items.q: Match each urinary RBC description with its label — 1) Crenated, isomorphic cells 2) Dysmorphic cells 3) Acanthocytes … A) "Mickey mouse" RBCs B) Urological category C) Nephrological category
items.exp: Urological: crenated, isomorphic; nephrological: dysmorphic; acanthocytes = Mickey mouse RBCs. (Book p743)

items.q: The nephrological RBCs nicknamed after a famous cartoon mouse are:
items.exp: Acanthocytes are called Mickey mouse RBCs, seen in the nephrological category. (Book p743)

items.q: Which statement about the leukocyte/nitrite dipstick for UTI is TRUE?
opts: It has high specificity but poor sensitivity
It has high sensitivity but poor specificity
It is equally sensitive and specific
items.exp: Leukocytes + nitrites for urinary tract infections: high specificity, poor sensitivity. (Book p743)

items.q: A positive urobilinogen pad on the dipstick points to:
items.exp: Urobilinogen on dipstick: extravascular hemolysis. (Book p743)

items.q: A type-2 diabetic started on an SGLT2 inhibitor shows urine ketones; the glycemic pattern the book pairs with this drug is:
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors: euglycemic ketosis (proximal RTA gives euglycemic glycosuria). (Book p743)

items.q: Euglycemic glycosuria on the dipstick glucose row is the marker of:
All of the following affect the leukocyte urine dipstick test EXCEPT:
items.exp: Listed factors: concentrated urine, high relative density, proteinuria, glucosuria, cephalothin & tetracycline, cephalexin, tobramycin. (Book p743)

items.q: Fill up: Cephalothin, tetracycline, cephalexin and tobramycin are listed as drugs affecting the urine ______ dipstick test.
items.exp: These drugs are listed under factors affecting the leukocyte urine dipstick test. (Book p743)

items.q: Which RBC-morphology statement is TRUE as per the figure?
opts: Crenated and isomorphic RBCs belong to the urological category
Crenated and isomorphic RBCs belong to the nephrological category
Dysmorphic RBCs belong to the urological category
items.exp: Urological: crenated, isomorphic; nephrological: dysmorphic, acanthocytes. (Book p743)
